summary: NOVA SPOT is a mobile-friendly interactive prototype designed to explore terrestrial environments as partial analogs for lunar and Martian field research. It organizes eight Earth locations and allows users to filter candidates by Moon or Mars relevance, inspect their environmental and geological characteristics, and compare them across four screening dimensions: terrain similarity, geological relevance, environmental harshness, and field-testing value. The prototype includes candidate profiles, a comparison matrix, and CSV export. Its purpose is to make early-stage analog screening transparent and understandable. details:
NOVA SPOT is an interactive, mobile-friendly prototype developed to support the early-stage identification and comparison of terrestrial environments that may serve as partial analogs for lunar and Martian exploration.

The prototype organizes eight Earth environments and allows users to explore their potential relevance to Moon and Mars research. Users can filter candidate locations, view individual site profiles, compare locations using a screening matrix, and export candidate information as a CSV file.

The screening framework considers four dimensions: terrain similarity, geological relevance, environmental harshness, and potential field-testing value. Each dimension uses a preliminary qualitative score from 1 to 5. The resulting index is intended for initial comparison only and is not a scientifically validated measurement.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with generative AI assistance for drafting and code generation. Its main benefit is to provide an accessible and transparent starting point for comparing potential terrestrial analog environments.

The current prototype does not claim to process satellite imagery or generate validated NASA-derived measurements. A future development stage will integrate documented Earth-observation and planetary datasets to produce reproducible, data-driven comparisons.
